newsitem.title: CHINA: China may set up Macau countdown clock after HK.
newsitem.headline: China may set up Macau countdown clock after HK.

text.p: China may set up a clock in Tiananmen Square to count down to the return of Macau after its Hong Kong clock ticks past zero to mark the British colony's reversion at midnight on Monday, officials said on Thursday.

"We are preparing to set up a new clock to countdown Macau's return from Portugal on December 20, 1999, but this has not been finally approved yet," said an official of the Xinhua news agency, one of the sponsors of the Hong Kong clock.

The Hongkong countdown clock was set up nearly three years ago in front of the Museum of Chinese History on the east side of Beijing's historic square and could be moved into a museum after Hongkong reverts to Chinese rule, he said.

China plans a huge celebration in front of the Hong Kong countdown clock on the night of June 30 to mark the end of more than 150 years of British colonial rule, including a spectacular fireworks show in the square.
